title: Ranking and unranking a spanning-tree Gray code
formal: Is there a uniformly polynomial-time rankable and unrankable edge-exchange ordering of the labeled spanning trees of K_n for every n≥2?
definitions: K_n is the simple complete graph on labels {1,…,n}. A spanning tree is represented by its n−1 unordered endpoint pairs in increasing lexicographic order. Let T_n be the set of these trees and M_n=|T_n|=n^(n−2). Seek bijections f_n:{0,…,M_n−1}→T_n such that consecutive trees have symmetric edge difference of size two. The list is a path: no last-to-first exchange is required. There must be two fixed deterministic Turing algorithms: given binary n and i, one outputs f_n(i); given n and a tree, the other outputs its unique i in binary. Each runs in n^{O(1)} bit operations, with a uniform exponent. Neither algorithm receives advice or an exponentially precomputed table. Invalid indices or invalid trees may be rejected.

context: The source distinguishes efficient traversal from the stronger ability to jump directly between a tree and its rank.

import_provenance.original_title: Ranking and unranking a spanning-tree Gray code
import_provenance.original_statement: Find an ordering of all spanning trees of the complete graph K_n in which successive trees exchange one edge and both ranking a tree and recovering the tree of a given rank take polynomial time in n. Such an ordering would combine minimal-change enumeration with efficient random access.

sentences: All labeled spanning trees of a complete graph must occur once.
A tree and its binary position must be convertible in polynomial time.
The same algorithms must work for every n without advice.
No cyclic adjacency of the endpoints is imposed.
